key_insight: ARGON makes neutral-atom compilation scalable by decoupling spatial conflict resolution from temporal routing and using a GNN to choose layouts that avoid future bottlenecks.
engineering_relevance: This framework helps quantum compiler designers generate collision-free transport schedules much faster while preserving parallelism and improving execution fidelity on large neutral-atom circuits.
method: Precompute an offline library of hardware-certified, high-parallelism spatial layouts.
Use a GNN to score candidate layouts based on deep temporal-horizon effects and avoid downstream routing bottlenecks.
Apply a heuristic router to convert the chosen layout sequence into collision-free physical atom transport.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports compilation in under 10 seconds, up to >10^4x speedup over the best baseline and about 600x average speedup, with up to 10^2x fidelity improvement on dense circuits.
watch_item: The approach depends on the quality and coverage of the offline layout library, so unusual hardware constraints or circuit patterns may require retraining or library expansion.
paper_title: ARGON: A GNN-Empowered Compilation Framework for Scalable Neutral Atom Computing
